synopsis: The recommended programme is a hybrid environment factory: parameterised representative sites anchored to surveyed real sites, with prototype tests measuring latency, detection-range correlation, brake timing, stopping dynamics, repeatability and model error [f76, f3705, f879]. Credibility should be quantified separately for each phenomenon using several metrics, not one universal score; the corpus reports no consensus on quantifying the domain gap and no accepted weather-realism score [f7468, f7552, f476, f11950]. Reported gaps are substantial but condition-specific: Sim2Radar produced 251 simulated versus 2,057 real points per frame across five indoor scenes, CropCraft reported a 9.9% average mIoU gap, and a November 2025 scan comparison reported DCD of 0.63 and segmentation mIoU of 21% [f3932, f3731, f4442]. Weather agreement depends on matching conditions: lidar rain mismatch increased with rain rate and depended on drop-size assumptions, while fog mismatch increased as visibility fell; realistic tracking outputs can also conceal large raw-data errors [f4414, f7556, f7557, f7821, f4540]. The main technical risk is the absence of a published quantitative off-road comparison of simulation-tuned brake thresholds against field results, alongside missing generic stopping-error benchmarks and validation gaps for dust, ultrasonic weather effects and thermal-camera conditions [f155, f251, f6094, f7561, f4581, f4591]. Physical confirmations should update discrepancy models rather than silently tune away errors, with comparisons at both sensor and perception-output levels; warning signs include no agreed correlation metrics by the first quarter of 2027, per-scene tuning, unreported residuals and uncertainty, and stalled or worsening held-out real performance [f7385, f11105, f10756, f10784].
